function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live weather data right now. If you’d like, I can give you a general idea of what the temperature tends to be in Moscow around this time of year, or help you find a reliable source where you can check the current conditions.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What weather is now in Moscow, in Celsius?" They want current temperature. We need to provide the answer. There's no tool for weather. So we just respond with the current temperature. But we don't have real-time data. We can approximate or say we can't fetch. But maybe we can use a placeholder. According to policy, we should not hallucinate. We can say we don't have real-time data. But we could also mention typical average. But better to say we cannot fetch. So respond: I don't have real-time data.
